_meta.note: round-2 canon: classic/traditional jokes, joke FORMATS (xiehouyu, Radio Yerevan, Beamten, doctor-doctor, oyaji gyagu, ajae, Monsieur-et-Madame, waiter, viola cycles) and industry folk humor recalled from Claude (claude-fable-5) training knowledge at user request; provenance per record is 'traditional/anonymous (Claude-recalled)' — verify attribution before republication; NOT scraped

text: 泥菩萨过江——自身难保 (ní púsà guò jiāng) — A clay bodhisattva crossing the river: can't even save itself.

meta.humor_hook: two-part allegorical saying: image sets the trap, tag springs it — the helper is the most helpless one present

text: 哑巴吃黄连——有苦说不出 (yǎba chī huánglián) — A mute eating bitter herb: suffering he cannot voice.

meta.humor_hook: the punch line names the exact clause the image already implied — recognition, not surprise

text: 猫哭老鼠——假慈悲 (māo kū lǎoshǔ) — The cat weeping for the mouse: fake compassion.

meta.humor_hook: predator grief as the universal emblem of performative sympathy

text: 黄鼠狼给鸡拜年——没安好心 (huángshǔláng gěi jī bàinián) — The weasel pays the hen a New Year visit: no good intentions.

meta.gloss: Season's greetings from your natural predator.
meta.humor_hook: etiquette used as camouflage — politeness itself becomes the tell

text: 秀才遇到兵——有理说不清 (xiùcai yù dào bīng) — When the scholar meets the soldier, reason cannot get through.

meta.gloss: Being right is not a weapons class.
meta.humor_hook: credentials collapse against force — the eternal meeting between logic and management

text: 千里送鹅毛——礼轻情意重 (qiān lǐ sòng émáo) — A goose feather carried a thousand li: the gift is light, the feeling heavy.

meta.gloss: Shipping cost exceeds item value; sentiment covers the difference.
meta.humor_hook: absurd logistics dignified by sincerity — the warm inversion of a scam

text: Radio Yerevan was asked: 'Is it true that cars are being given away on Red Square in Moscow?' — 'In principle yes. But it is not Moscow, it is Leningrad; not cars but bicycles; and they are not being given away, they are being stolen.'

meta.humor_hook: the correction format: confirm the frame, then swap every load-bearing fact one at a time

text: Radio Yerevan was asked: 'Could a nuclear war destroy our beloved Yerevan?' — 'In principle yes. But Baku is an even more beautiful city.'

meta.humor_hook: answering a question of survival as a question of rivalry — priorities revealed under the mushroom cloud

text: Radio Yerevan was asked: 'What is the difference between the Constitution and reality?' — 'In principle, nothing: both guarantee freedom of speech. The Constitution, however, does not guarantee freedom after the speech.'

meta.origin: Soviet-era joke cycle (translated; circulated in many variants)
meta.humor_hook: one preposition carries the whole regime — 'of' versus 'after'

text: We pretend to work, and they pretend to pay us.

meta.humor_hook: perfect symmetry of mutual fraud stated as a stable equilibrium

text: Under capitalism, man exploits man. Under socialism, it is exactly the other way around.

meta.humor_hook: the reversal that changes nothing — grammar promises difference, semantics delivers identity

text: A man sees a queue forming and joins it immediately. Only then does he ask the person in front: 'What are they selling?' — 'No idea, but why risk missing it?'

meta.humor_hook: scarcity trains reflexes that skip the question entirely — the queue is the product

text: Warum können Beamte nicht Verstecken spielen? — Weil niemand sie sucht. (Why can't civil servants play hide-and-seek? Because nobody would look for them.)

meta.humor_hook: the children's game rule collides with institutional indifference

text: Drei Leute sitzen im Büro, einer arbeitet: zwei Beamte und ein Ventilator. (Three in the office and one of them works: two civil servants and a fan.)

meta.humor_hook: the census format — the appliance out-performs the staff on the third beat

text: Kommt ein Bürger ins Amt: 'Arbeiten hier auch Menschen?' — 'Nein, nur Beamte.' (A citizen enters the office: 'Do any humans work here?' — 'No, only civil servants.')

meta.humor_hook: the clerk volunteers the insult about himself as a correction of category

text: My dog's got no nose. — How does it smell? — Terrible!

meta.humor_hook: the question means 'perceive odor', the answer means 'emit odor' — a verb with two doors

text: Doctor, doctor, I feel like a pair of curtains. — Pull yourself together!

meta.humor_hook: the idiom for composure is also the literal instruction for drapery

text: Doctor, doctor, everyone keeps ignoring me. — Next, please!

meta.humor_hook: the reply performs the complaint instead of treating it

text: Doctor, doctor, I keep thinking I'm invisible. — Who said that?

meta.humor_hook: the diagnosis is granted by the doctor's failure to see the patient

text: Shlof gikher, me darf di kishns. — Sleep faster, we need the pillows.

meta.humor_hook: an unhurryable activity given a production quota — scarcity logic applied to dreams

text: If the rich could hire other people to die for them, the poor could make a wonderful living.

meta.humor_hook: extends outsourcing to the one task that cannot be delegated, and finds the labor market for it instantly

text: A shlimazl falls on his back and breaks his nose.

meta.origin: Yiddish folk saying (translated; shlimazl = the chronically unlucky)
meta.humor_hook: bad luck so committed it violates anatomy

text: 布団が吹っ飛んだ (futon ga futtonda) — The futon blew away.

meta.gloss: 'futon' hides inside the verb 'futtonda' (blew off) — the classic Japanese dad pun.
meta.humor_hook: the object of the sentence is phonetically trapped inside its own verb

text: アルミ缶の上にあるみかん (arumikan no ue ni aru mikan) — The mandarin orange on top of the aluminum can.

meta.gloss: 'arumikan' (aluminum can) contains 'aru mikan' (there is a mandarin).
meta.humor_hook: one sound-string parses two ways and the sentence stages both readings at once

text: イクラはいくら? (ikura wa ikura?) — How much is the salmon roe?

meta.humor_hook: a homophone interrogates itself at the fish counter

text: 세상에서 제일 뜨거운 과일은? 천도복숭아. (The hottest fruit in the world? The cheondo peach.)

meta.gloss: 'cheondo' names the peach variety and sounds like 'a thousand degrees'.
meta.humor_hook: a quiz-format pun where produce is assigned a temperature by homophony

text: 세종대왕이 만든 우유는? 아야어여오요우유. (The milk King Sejong invented? A-ya-eo-yeo-o-yo-u-yu.)

meta.gloss: recites the Korean vowel order, which happens to end in 'uyu' — milk.
meta.humor_hook: the alphabet lesson smuggles the product name in its final syllables

text: Monsieur et Madame Térieur ont deux fils : Alain et Alex. (Mr. and Mrs. Térieur have two sons: Alain and Alex — 'à l'intérieur' and 'à l'extérieur', inside and outside.)

meta.humor_hook: given names assemble with the surname into ordinary phrases — the family tree is a pun generator

text: Monsieur et Madame Provisation ont un fils : Jim. (Mr. and Mrs. Provisation have a son: Jim — 'Jim Provisation' = improvisation.)

meta.humor_hook: the pun only fires when the listener says the full name aloud — the audience does the assembly

text: ¿Cómo se dice pañuelo en japonés? Saka-moko. (How do you say handkerchief in Japanese? 'Saka-moko' — sounds like 'saca moco', snot-remover.)

meta.humor_hook: fake-translation format: foreign phonology as a costume for a rude Spanish phrase

text: ¿Qué le dice un jaguar a otro jaguar? Jaguar you. (What does one jaguar say to another? 'Jaguar you' — 'how are you'.)

meta.humor_hook: the animal's name is repurposed as English small talk — bilingual homophony as the whole engine

text: Perché i carabinieri girano in coppia? Perché uno sa leggere e l'altro sa scrivere. (Why do carabinieri patrol in pairs? One knows how to read, the other how to write.)

meta.origin: Italian institutional joke cycle (traditional; punches at the state police as an institution)
meta.humor_hook: division of labor presented as full coverage — the pair sums to one literate person

text: O que o pato disse para a pata? Vem quá! (What did the drake say to the duck? 'Come here' — 'quá' is both 'here' colloquially and the quack sound.)

meta.humor_hook: the mating call and the imperative share one syllable — onomatopoeia doubles as grammar

text: Juha lost his donkey and ran through the village shouting thanks to God. 'Why give thanks?' they asked. 'Because I was not riding it — otherwise I would be lost too.'

meta.humor_hook: impeccable logic applied one frame too wide — gratitude computed from the wrong premise

text: Nasreddin borrowed a cauldron and returned it with a small pot inside: 'Your cauldron gave birth.' The neighbor happily kept both. Next time, Nasreddin did not return the cauldron at all: 'Your cauldron died.' — 'Cauldrons don't die!' — 'You believed it gave birth.'

meta.humor_hook: the victim's greed ratifies the absurd premise, which then executes against him

text: Emperor Akbar asked Birbal how many crows were in Agra. 'Twenty-one thousand, five hundred and twenty-three,' said Birbal. 'And if there are more?' — 'Then relatives are visiting.' — 'And fewer?' — 'Some have gone to visit relatives.'

meta.humor_hook: an unfalsifiable answer engineered with a straight face — precision as the costume of wit

text: What's the difference between a viola and an onion? Nobody cries when you chop up a viola.

meta.origin: orchestral musicians' joke cycle (traditional in-group humor)
meta.humor_hook: the comparison format promises sympathy and delivers an inventory of who gets none

text: How do you keep your violin from getting stolen? Keep it in a viola case.

meta.origin: orchestral musicians' joke cycle (traditional in-group humor)
meta.humor_hook: security through stigma — the case itself is the anti-theft device

text: What do you call a drummer who just broke up with his girlfriend? Homeless.

meta.origin: band musicians' joke cycle (traditional in-group humor)
meta.humor_hook: the economic punchline arrives disguised as a relationship question

text: Ninety-nine percent of lawyers give the rest a bad name.

meta.humor_hook: the cliché runs in reverse — the bad apples are the barrel

text: What's the difference between a good lawyer and a great lawyer? A good lawyer knows the law. A great lawyer knows the judge.

meta.humor_hook: the ladder of merit tops out in nepotism — expertise loses to acquaintance

text: The operation was a complete success. Unfortunately, the patient died.

meta.humor_hook: success redefined by the metric that excludes the outcome

text: I have good news and bad news. The good news is they're naming a disease after you.

meta.humor_hook: immortality granted through the worst possible channel — fame and diagnosis fused

text: A good landing is one you can walk away from. A great landing is one where they can use the airplane again.

meta.humor_hook: the quality scale quietly admits the plane is usually the casualty

text: Helicopters don't really fly. They're just so ugly the earth repels them.

meta.humor_hook: aerodynamics replaced by aesthetics as the load-bearing force

text: The optimist says the glass is half full. The pessimist says the glass is half empty. The engineer says the glass is twice as big as it needs to be.

meta.humor_hook: the philosophical dichotomy is dissolved by a spec review

text: A statistician drowned crossing a river that was, on average, three feet deep.

meta.humor_hook: the summary statistic commits the murder — aggregation hides the fatal tail

text: Ask an accountant what two plus two is, and the accountant closes the blinds and whispers: 'What do you want it to be?'

meta.humor_hook: arithmetic revealed as a negotiable service — the whisper does half the work

text: A consultant is someone who borrows your watch to tell you the time — and then keeps the watch.

meta.humor_hook: the service is assembled entirely from the client's own assets, billed, then expropriated

text: Drill sergeant: 'I didn't see you at camouflage training this morning!' Recruit: 'Thank you, sir!'

meta.humor_hook: the reprimand is indistinguishable from the course's own success criterion

text: If your mother says she loves you, check it out.

meta.origin: City News Bureau of Chicago newsroom maxim (institutional folk)
meta.humor_hook: professional skepticism escalated past the last plausible target

text: Waiter, what's this fly doing in my soup? — The backstroke, sir.

meta.humor_hook: the complaint's idiom is answered as a literal activity report

text: Waiter, will my pizza be long? — No sir, it will be round.

meta.humor_hook: the temporal question is intercepted by geometry

text: How do you make a small fortune in farming? Start with a large fortune.

meta.origin: farming/aviation/wine folk joke (traditional; the frame migrates across capital-hungry industries)
meta.humor_hook: the get-rich formula parses as its own bankruptcy report

text: What time do you go to the dentist? Tooth-hurty.

meta.humor_hook: the clock and the symptom collapse into one phrase

text: A SQL query walks into a bar, goes up to two tables and asks: 'May I join you?'

meta.humor_hook: the database verb is also the social verb — jargon walks into an idiom

text: There's no place like 127.0.0.1.

meta.humor_hook: the homesick proverb resolves to localhost — sentiment with a loopback address

text: PEBKAC: problem exists between keyboard and chair.

meta.humor_hook: the diagnostic locates the fault by coordinates and lets the listener compute who sits there

text: The best thing about academia is the flexibility: you can work any eighty hours a week you want.

meta.origin: academic/startup folk joke (traditional; the frame migrates)
meta.humor_hook: freedom is real, only the quantity was a trap

text: Geologists are great at finding faults.

meta.humor_hook: the technical term and the marital complaint share a spelling

text: An actuary is someone who wanted to be an accountant but couldn't handle the excitement.

meta.humor_hook: a profession famous for caution is used as the thrill-seeking baseline

text: Give a man a fish and he eats for a day. Teach a man to fish and he sits in a boat drinking beer all day.

meta.humor_hook: the uplift proverb is honored letter-for-letter while its spirit files a complaint
